newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian airlines to treble fares.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian airlines to treble fares.

text.p: Nigerias airlines announced on Thursday they will raise domestic air fares by 200 percent from Monday.
Elijah Omokhodion, chairman of the Nigerian Airline Operators (AON), said in a statement that this was the only way to keep the airline industry healthy.
"AON has decided that from Monday, February 17, all member airlines will adjust their fares by 200 percent," the statement said.
It means an economy one-way ticket to the capital Abuja from Lagos, a distance of about 800 km (500 miles), would cost 7,920 naira ($99), three times the current price of 2,685 naira ($33.56).
Aviation ministry officials were not immediately available to comment on the fare hike.
In November, the military government cancelled what it called an "insensitive" 100 percent increase in domestic air fares annnounced by AON.
The airlines have long campaigned for an increase in domestic airfares, saying it was the only way to sustain their operations in an economy that has been in recession for years.
Government announced in this years fiscal budget in January that airline operators would no longer pay tariffs on aircraft spare parts.
The AON statement said: "The exemption granted by government would lower operation costs but would not bring any significant impact on the fortunes of the airlines.
"It is only with 200 percent increase that we can earn enough to keep our craft in good state and maintain high safety standards."
The spate of air accidents in Nigeria since last year has given people cause for worry. Aviation experts blamed the accidents on the tight financial squeeze in the industry.

The experts have dubbed many aircraft operated in Nigeria "flying coffins" because of the lack of maintenance and the fact that many are from former communist countries with manuals in languages foreign to Nigerian pilots.
